dataSources: SC4S Meraki vendor pack (sourcetype=meraki) for MR access-point syslog and/or Splunk Add-on for Cisco WLC (sourcetype=cisco:wlc:syslog) for AireOS/Catalyst 9800 syslog. NOTE: ssid and client_mac are NOT auto-extracted on sourcetype=meraki; this UC uses rex to pull them from the structured key=value Meraki payload (vap=, aid=, src=) and the freeform Cisco WLC body. ot_wireless_allowlist.csv is a customer-maintained allowlist with columns (client_mac, asset_class).
spl:
index=wireless (sourcetype="meraki" OR sourcetype="cisco:wlc:syslog") earliest=-24h
| rex "(?:vap='|ssid='|SSID )(?<ssid>[A-Za-z0-9_\-\.]+)"
| rex "(?:client_mac=|aid='|MAC )(?<client_mac>[0-9A-Fa-f:]+)"
| rex "(?:src=|src_ip=)(?<src_ip>[\d\.]+)"
| where like(ssid, "OT-PROD-%")
| iplocation src_ip
| lookup ot_wireless_allowlist.csv client_mac OUTPUT asset_class
| where asset_class!="instrumentation" OR isnull(asset_class)
| stats earliest(_time) as first_seen,
        latest(_time) as last_seen,
        values(asset_class) as asset_classes
         by client_mac, ssid, host
| sort - last_seen

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: WLAN controller syslog (Splunkbase).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: SC4S Meraki vendor pack (sourcetype=meraki) for MR access-point syslog and/or Splunk Add-on for Cisco WLC (sourcetype=cisco:wlc:syslog) for AireOS/Catalyst 9800 syslog. NOTE: ssid and client_mac are NOT auto-extracted on sourcetype=meraki; this UC uses rex to pull them from the structured key=value Meraki payload (vap=, aid=, src=) and the freeform Cisco WLC body. ot_wireless_allowlist.csv is a customer-maintained allowlist with columns (client_mac, asset_class)..
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
1. Configure SC4S to receive Meraki MR and/or Cisco WLC syslog. 2. Use rex to extract ssid, client_mac, src_ip — these are not auto-parsed fields on either sourcetype. 3. Maintain ot_wireless_allowlist.csv with the MAC addresses of authorised OT instrumentation. 4. The query surfaces clients on OT-PROD-* SSIDs that are not in the allowlist or are tagged as a non-instrumentation asset class. 5. For OUI-based vendor categorisation, supplement with an OUI lookup against the IEEE registry.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=wireless (sourcetype="meraki" OR sourcetype="cisco:wlc:syslog") earliest=-24h
| rex "(?:vap='|ssid='|SSID )(?<ssid>[A-Za-z0-9_\-\.]+)"
| rex "(?:client_mac=|aid='|MAC )(?<client_mac>[0-9A-Fa-f:]+)"
| rex "(?:src=|src_ip=)(?<src_ip>[\d\.]+)"
| where like(ssid, "OT-PROD-%")
| iplocation src_ip
| lookup ot_wireless_allowlist.csv client_mac OUTPUT asset_class
| where asset_class!="instrumentation" OR isnull(asset_class)
| stats earliest(_time) as first_seen,
        latest(_time) as last_seen,
        values(asset_class) as asset_classes
         by client_mac, ssid, host
| sort - last_seen
```

Understanding this SPL

**Wireless Zone Security Monitoring — Unknown Clients on OT SSID** — Gives the responsible team auditor-ready evidence for IEC 62443 compliance by automating regulatory compliance evidence using indexes wireless and sourcetypes cisco:wlc:syslog, meraki:association. Replaces manual evidence gathering with a continuous Splunk search that produces structured, time-stamped artefacts suitable for regulatory examination and internal audit review.

Documented **Data sources**: SC4S Meraki vendor pack (sourcetype=meraki) for MR access-point syslog and/or Splunk Add-on for Cisco WLC (sourcetype=cisco:wlc:syslog) for AireOS/Catalyst 9800 syslog. NOTE: ssid and client_mac are NOT auto-extracted on sourcetype=meraki; this UC uses rex to pull them from the structured key=value Meraki payload (vap=, aid=, src=) and the freeform Cisco WLC body. ot_wireless_allowlist.csv is a customer-maintained allowlist with columns (client_mac, asset_class). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): WLAN controller syslog (Splunkbase). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: wireless; **sourcetype**: meraki, cisco:wlc. Those sourcetypes align with what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=wireless, sourcetype="meraki", time bounds. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• Extracts fields with `rex` (regular expression).
• Extracts fields with `rex` (regular expression).

Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Table, Map, Time chart. Key fields: `ap_name`, `client_mac`, `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `ssid`.

**Ecosystem integration:** Forward compliance detections to Splunk SOAR for automated incident triage and escalation playbooks. Enrich events with asset context from ServiceNow CMDB. Cross-reference with CrowdStrike Falcon or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint for host forensics and threat detection context. Integrate Okta or Azure AD identity context to determine if the acting user had appropriate authorisation. Feed validated findings into the GRC platform (e.g., RSA Archer, ServiceNow GRC, or AuditBoard) for regulatory compliance tracking and audit evidence management.
